official.status_note: The DCU International Scholarships for Non-EU Students 2027-28 page is live and lists the eligible programmes and reductions for each faculty for the 2027-28 academic year.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Each award is a reduction of the full-time 2027-2028 Non-EU Tuition fee, applied directly to the student account. The page describes these as partial merit-based scholarships.

official.description: Dublin City University offers partial merit-based international scholarships to non-EU students across its faculties and the DCU Business School for the 2027-28 academic year. Applicants are automatically considered when they apply as a non-EU student, only successful recipients are notified by email, and the reduction is applied directly to the student account.
official.program_type: Partial merit-based international tuition fee scholarship for non-EU students
official.english_requirement: Applicants whose first language is not English must provide evidence of competence in English in a recognised English language test. DCU's published minimum standards are IELTS Academic composite 6.5 with no less than 6.0 in any one component, TOEFL iBT total score 92, PTE Academic 63 with a minimum of 59 in all components, or Duolingo 120 overall with at least 110 in each subscore; the Cambridge English scale minimum is 180 with no less than 169 in each skill (changing to 176+ for entry 2027). Requirements are higher in some faculties - DCU Business School and the School of Communications require 6.5 in writing and speaking - and individual programmes may require more. Certificates must be awarded within two years prior to the programme start date, and all scores must be achieved in one sitting.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no scholarship application to write: DCU automatically considers every non-EU application to a listed 2027-28 programme, so the only thing you control is which programme code you apply to and how strong that application is. The money varies sharply by faculty and level, from 1,850 euro in Humanities and Social Sciences undergraduate to 6,100 euro in Science and Health undergraduate, so faculty choice is the single biggest lever on the value you receive. Because you are only told if you succeeded, and because a DCU International scholarship rules out any other DCU scholarship such as a Merit Scholarship, you should model the worst case where you receive nothing and treat any reduction as a bonus against a fee you have already budgeted.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong non-EU applicants applying to a listed 2027-28 full-time programme in Science and Health, Engineering or Computing, where the reductions are largest.
application_readiness_checklist: Look up your exact programme code on the relevant faculty's 2027-28 eligible list before applying - if the code is absent, no scholarship applies to you
Compare the reduction on offer across faculties for the kind of programme you want; the same discipline can be worth thousands more in a different faculty
Note the exceptions - DC204 BSc in Athletic Therapy and Training carries 3,100 euro rather than 6,100 euro, and two Science and Health master's programmes carry 4,500 rather than 5,000 euro
Upload your English language test evidence at application, because DCU will not assess the application until all required documentation is received
Check your faculty's specific English thresholds - DCU Business School and the School of Communications require 6.5 in writing and speaking, above the general 6.0 component minimum
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme not on the 2027-28 eligible list for your faculty, which excludes you from consideration entirely
Submitting without English language evidence, since the application will not be assessed until it is received
Falsified supporting documents, which DCU reserves the right to act on by withdrawing or rescinding an application or offer at any stage
Assuming an English certificate older than two years will count - it will not
Assuming you can stack this with a DCU Merit Scholarship; a DCU International scholarship excludes consideration for another DCU scholarship
Expecting an application to a part-time programme to qualify, since the reductions apply to full-time 2027-28 Non-EU tuition fees
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything the reduction does not cover: the remainder of the 2027-28 Non-EU tuition fee, living costs, accommodation and travel. The Science and Health and Engineering reductions of 5,000 to 6,100 euro are the largest, but the underlying non-EU fee is still the applicant's to fund in part.
document_audit: Your English test result must come from a single sitting - combined scores from different dates are not accepted
If you are awaiting a final English test result, DCU allows a holding document naming the test and expected result date, but only if you follow that process; otherwise the application sits unassessed
Programme pages may set English requirements above the general minimum, so check your specific programme page rather than the general table
Verification checks are carried out on documents supporting eligibility, so transcripts and certificates must be genuine and issued by the awarding body
alerts: Recipients are notified by email only, so silence is not a decision and a noisy inbox is a real risk
The reduction is applied directly to the student account rather than paid to you, so it reduces what you owe rather than giving you cash in hand
A DCU International scholarship cannot be combined with another DCU scholarship, which can make accepting the smaller award strategically worse than holding out for the Merit Scholarship
The page is specific to 2027-28 and was recently updated; do not rely on the previous year's programme code list
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through the DCU Student Application Portal as a non-EU student to an eligible 2027-28 programme; consideration is automatic, and any reduction is confirmed by email and credited directly to the student account.
